title: Light
exclusionReason: No side-view camera available (standard or optional)
driverAssistBrand: Kia Drive Wise (Highway Driving Assist 2 on higher trims)
infotainment: Panoramic dual 12.3-inch curved displays (digital cluster + center touch), Kia Connected Services, native maps, OTA capable. Source: https://www.kia.com/us/en/ev6/specs-compare
adasStandard: Standard Kia Drive Wise: Forward Collision-Avoidance Assist (FCA) with pedestrian / cyclist detection, Lane Keeping Assist (LKA), Lane Following Assist (LFA), Driver Attention Warning (DAW), Smart Cruise Control (SCC) w/ stop-and-go, Blind-Spot Collision-Avoidance Assist (BCA), Rear Cross-Traffic Collision-Avoidance Assist (RCCA), High Beam Assist, Safe Exit Warning. Source: https://www.kia.com/us/en/ev6/specs-compare
adasOptional: Highway Driving Assist 2 (HDA2 — hands-on lane-centering w/ machine-learning lane-change assist) on Wind+; Remote Smart Parking Assist 2 (RSPA2) on GT-Line. Source: https://www.kia.com/us/en/ev6/specs-compare
rearViewCameraNotes: Standard rear-view camera with dynamic guidelines. Resolution not separately specified by Kia; integrated into the 12.3-inch infotainment display. Source: https://www.kia.com/us/en/ev6/specs-compare
sideViewCameraNotes: Surround View Monitor (360-camera) and Blind-Spot View Monitor (live-feed side cameras in the instrument cluster when turn signal is activated) are restricted to GT-Line on MY2025; not available on Light. Source: https://www.kia.com/us/en/ev6/specs-compare
subscriptionFeatures: Kia Connect tiers (free 3-yr trial then paid): Connect Light (free; basic emergency assistance), Connect ~$14.99/mo or $149/yr (remote start, remote climate, remote seat heat/vent, find-my-car, curfew alerts, OTA), Connect+ ~$24.99/mo (Wi-Fi hotspot data; data plan separate). Lapsed subscription: vehicle still drives normally, only the remote/connected layer disables. Source: https://owners.kia.com/us/en/uvo-compare-packages.html
drmNotes: Vehicle drives, climate-controls, infotainment-on-USB, CarPlay/Android Auto (wired), DC fast charging via plug-in card or NACS adapter all work without an internet connection. Kia Connect (remote start, remote climate, OTA updates, Plug & Charge on Tesla Superchargers, stolen-vehicle services) requires a cellular link and an active subscription (complimentary 3 years on new purchase). No history of Kia remotely disabling shipped features. Source: https://owners.kia.com/us/en/about-uvo-link.html
killSwitchNotes: No hardware impaired-driving kill switch. Driver Attention Warning is camera+steering-input based, software-only, warns via chime/visual cue — does not disable the vehicle. Source: https://www.kia.com/us/en/adas.html
knownIssues: ICCU (Integrated Charging Control Unit) failures reported on early E-GMP vehicles (2022-2023 EV6/Ioniq 5) — Kia issued recall 24V-321 and a software update; MY2025 builds use revised ICCU hardware. Forum reports of occasional 12V battery drain when sitting unused for weeks. Sources: https://insideevs.com/news/715823/hyundai-kia-iccu-recall/ , https://www.nhtsa.gov/recalls
recalls: NHTSA recall lookup current as of 2026-05-21; MY2025 EV6 affected by carryover ICCU campaign 24V-321 (for early production), and a separate seat-belt-pretensioner inspection campaign. Use https://www.nhtsa.gov/recalls with the VIN for live status.
stateIncentives: Varies by state. Most generous: CA CVRP up to $2,000 (income-qualified), CO state tax credit $5,000, NJ ZEV sales-tax exemption, NY Drive Clean rebate up to $2,000. Federal $7,500 IRA tax credit not available for MY2025 EV6 (built in Korea, fails final-assembly requirement); leases can still pass through the commercial credit. Source: https://www.fueleconomy.gov/feg/taxevb.shtml
